name: Fourthwall
tagline: Creator storefronts, merchandise, memberships, donations, and fulfillment

pricing.native: No monthly fee; product and payment fees apply
pricing.notes: The pricing model is not safely comparable as one fixed monthly USD amount. Review the official source before publication.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 5 GB digital storage; 2 team members; 5% fee on digital products and memberships; 0% on catalog merch, self-shipped products and tips.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 100 GB digital storage; unlimited team members; 0% digital-product fee; 5% memberships fee; $10 sample credit per month.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom storage, teams and commercial terms; 0 self-serve prices published.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 5 GB digital storage, 2 team members, 5% digital-product and membership fees, and 0% fees on catalog/self-shipped products and tips
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual for Pro; Free is transaction-based
pricing.hiddenCosts: US card processing is 2.9% + $0.30; catalog merchandise production, fulfillment and shipping are deducted separately; memberships retain a 5% platform fee even on Pro.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Fourthwall's durable value is payments, network, compliance, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a narrow creator commerce storefront or member area for one creator, using Stripe Checkout and explicit digital-delivery rules.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: Stripe account and API keys in .env
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: tax, disputes, payouts, and fraud operations
whyPeopleStillPay: Fourthwall: Creators pay to outsource payments, tax complexity, disputes, deliverability, moderation, and the trust needed to convert strangers.
ongoingBurden: Own payments, webhooks, refunds, tax records, fraud, access control, file delivery, moderation, backups, and support.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Ghost
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Membership posts are real; merchandise production, fulfilment and donations are entirely somebody else's problem.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Medusa
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A backend developers can assemble into commerce, with no creator storefront, fulfilment network or painless setup.

rejectedAlternatives.name: WooCommerce
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A store, not a print-on-demand fulfilment service or creator membership platform; the missing half is the expensive half.

notes: Credibility row: Fourthwall survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Fourthwall; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + PostgreSQL + Stripe.
Primary job: Build a narrow creator commerce storefront or member area for one creator, using Stripe Checkout and explicit digital-delivery rules.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: marketplace discovery and buyer trust; tax, disputes, payouts, and fraud operations; native apps and community moderation.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
